newsitem.title: HUNGARY: IMF team says Hungary economy on track.
newsitem.headline: IMF team says Hungary economy on track.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF), ending an overview of a loan to Hungary, found the economy on track but warned that the social security deficit was larger than planned, the Finance Ministry said.
A visiting IMF delegation finished the third overview of a 264.18 million SDR, 23-month stand-by loan facility to Hungary on Wednesday, the ministry said.
"The IMF delegation regarded the economy's performance in the first quarter of the year as positive," the ministry said.
The IMF had said most of Hungary's economic figures met the targets, but the social security budget remained a sensitive area.

"According to their opinion economic growth, the deficits of the current account and of the budget, and the moderation of inflation this year are in harmony with targets of the programme set for this year and substantial results have been reached in structural reforms," the ministry said.
"However, the deficit of the social security funds differs from the forecast."
The government said recently that the social security deficit was likely to overshoot the 13.5 billion target for 1997 by some 20 billion forints.
The ministry said the government would take measures to improve the collection of social security contributions and cut expenditures of social security funds.
However, looking at the whole government budget, the opinion of the IMF delegation was positive, the ministry said.
"The sides agreed that the direction of fiscal policies is appropriate to keep the budget deficit on target."
Hungary plans a government budget deficit of 4.9 percent of gross domestic product for this year.
The country targets up to three percent GDP growth in 1997, after preliminary one percent growth in 1996 and plans to cut average inflation to around 18 percent from 23.6 percent last year.

The government forecast the current account deficit to widen to $2 billion in 1997 from $1.7 billion in 1996, while it sees a trade deficit between $2.5 billion and $3 billion, compared with $2.7 billion last year.

The now completed third IMF review was the last overview of the loan facility which expires in February 1998, the ministry said, adding that the delegates were expected to submit their report to the IMF board in September.
"The successful (economic) stabilisation makes the signing of a new agreement with the IMF unnecessary ," the ministry said.
Hungary declared when signing the agreement that it did not plan to draw the loan and it reiterated this position, the ministry said.
